questions.prompt: An object's x-position over five frames is 0,1,2,3,4 in clip A and 4,3,2,1,0 in clip B. Which feature separates the clips?
options: The maximum x over the clip.
The mean difference between consecutive frames.
The mean of the per-frame x (bag of frames).
questions.explanation: The bag mean is 2 for both and the max is 4 for both; the mean consecutive difference is +1 versus -1.

questions.prompt: A 150-frame clip is sampled with 6 segment-centre indices. What is the last index?
A 28 Hz periodic motion is filmed at 30 fps. What apparent frequency (Hz) does it have?
To avoid aliasing a 12 Hz periodic motion, the camera rate must be
options: any rate, since video is continuous
questions.explanation: Nyquist: sample at more than twice the highest frequency.

questions.prompt: Stride-3 sampling of 8 frames at 30 fps starting at frame 0 covers how many seconds? (3 decimals)
A Lucas-Kanade window lies on a long straight vertical edge. What is the consequence?
questions.skillLabel: Optical flow and the aperture problem
options: The flow is recovered exactly, since the edge gives strong gradients.
The window is too small, so the 2x2 matrix is dominated by noise.
Only the flow component normal to the edge is recoverable (aperture problem).
Only the component along the edge is measured, so the flow is vertical.
questions.explanation: All gradients are parallel, so the 2x2 matrix is singular.

questions.prompt: Design an experiment that shows whether a robot task (e.g. recognising a door opening versus closing) needs a temporal model. State the baseline, the test set, a boundary case and a rejection rule.
rubric: Defines a frame-only baseline and a temporal model on the same frames.
Includes a reversal or ambiguity test set and a still-scene boundary case.
States that if the frame-only model matches on the ambiguity set, time is not needed.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
